correctness.rationale: The positive Gram determinant and signed eigenvalue region were checked. Convexity under orthogonal swapping yields global symmetry reduction, and the exact 2+1 eigenvalues give a scalar ratio minimization. The 2x2 condition number has unique minimum \(q=1+d\); the other eigenmode is fixed at 1-d. Their unique crossing produces the stated threshold, and common scaling realizes the bound. Boundary agreement and 24,005 independent finite numerical comparisons were checked; numerical checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The explicit three-row, two-branch global weight-ratio optimizer and its sharp spectral-mode switch are not present in the fully inspected recent Cimmino source, whose general-n theorem optimizes only a fixed weight ray. General prior diagonal preconditioning algorithms do not state the closed form. Classical optimal-scaling special cases, especially older inaccessible full texts, remain a residual historical priority risk; this is best-knowledge originality, not proven uniqueness.
residual_risks: Shapiro (1985) expressly discusses closed-form optimal symmetric scaling special cases, but its full text could not be inspected; an equivalent statement or a dominating special-case theorem may exist.
Kolotilina (2002) characterizes best conditioned block matrices, but only abstract material was accessible.
Indexed and semantic searches cannot rule out all older books, unnamed matrix inequalities or unindexed equivalent formulations.

value.rationale: This is the first twofold-symmetric three-row extension beyond the recently solved two-row weight problem. It gives globally optimal constructive positive weights, a sharp and interpretable active-eigenmode transition, and a real convergence-factor improvement (\(15/29\) instead of \((1+\sqrt 3)/4\) for an explicit rational example). The geometry is natural and the phase is nontrivial; no larger-dimensional or practical speedup is claimed.
